decisions.quote: Anderson and Raney (2018) explored this in an experimental study ( n = 234) and found evidence of the Black criminal stereotype among sports fans. However, more research was needed to further explore this phenomenon. The current study employed a similar experimental design ( n = 603) in an attempt to (1) replicate their 2018 study to examine whether sports fans’ perceptions of criminal athletes have changed over the past several years, especially in light of the Black Lives Matter movement, and (2) determine whether the sport played by an alleged criminal athlete might be linked to judgments regarding race and crime in sports.
decisions.reason: The expert’s missing-print-date and missing-n234 objections no longer apply. The raw original DOI record confirms print June2018 versus online June2017 and directly reports experimental n234 and evidence of the Black criminal stereotype among sports fans. These match the current explicitly named Anderson/Raney2018 n234 study; the current n603 experiment retests that finding. The current deposited reference list also includes the exact shipped DOI. Together this identifies row2427 as the named original rather than an invented second2018 paper. raw_expert_opinion.reason: No prior adjudication or state file exists for this work. The abstract explicitly reports an experimental replication (n = 603) of an earlier experimental study by Anderson and Raney (2018) (n = 234) on sports fandom and the Black criminal stereotype. Shipped row 2427 is Anderson and Raney (2017), 'Exploring the Relationship Between Sports Fandom and the Black Criminal Stereotype' (DOI 10.1177/2167479517713152), which Crossref metadata shows was published online June 29, 2017 in Communication & Sport, vol. 6, issue 3, pp. 263-282. Because the supplied primary source is abstract-only without a reference list and the supplied Crossref record gives only the 2017 publication date without confirming a 2018 print issue year or the n = 234 sample size, the unresolved question is whether 'Anderson and Raney (2018)' is the print-issue citation of shipped row 2427 or a separate 2018 report.
